headline: ULTIMATUM TO HOLLAND
body: THE HAGUE, May 10. The ultimatum was made while the invasion was already taking place. Queen Wilhelmina issued a proclamation to the people: 'I herewith launch a flaming protest against this unprecedented violation of all that is decent among cultured States.'
signals: NAZIS DEMAND IMMEDIATE SURRENDER OF HOLLAND

headline: ALLIES CONTINUE THEIR WITHDRAWAL TO COAST
body: It is officially stated that the B.E.F. and the French in the north have been forced to fall back towards the coast in view of the increased German pressure on the northern and southern flanks in the battle now raging. The operation is being carried out with great skill and daring, and the troops not immediately engaged are being evacuated.
signals: SMALL BRITISH FORCE MAKES HEROIC STAND AT CALAIS

headline: EPIC OF EVACUATION
body: LONDON, June 4. The epic of the evacuation from Dunkirk, the success of which continued so much greater than was hoped for, is being hailed throughout Britain by all organisations and leaders, including this morning the House of Commons.

headline: 'FINEST HOUR'
body: RUGBY, June 18. The Prime Minister, Mr. Churchill, in a broadcast speech this evening discussed, in much the same terms as he had done earlier in his House of Commons statement, the possibilities of the invasion of Britain by an enemy. The Dominions stand united in the grave crisis.
signals: EMPIRE TO PERSEVERE TO THE END

headline: FRENCH SURRENDER NOW COMPLETE
body: It is officially stated at Rome that an armistice has been signed and hostilities cease at 1.35 a.m., Italian time. A radio report says that France and Italy signed the armistice in Rome at 5.35 p.m. Greenwich mean time.

headline: R.A.F. FIGHTERS DOWN GERMAN RAIDERS
body: Besides the five German bombers destroyed in to-day's air raids on Britain four more 'planes were also damaged. The raids were of the hit and run type, and in most cases the Nazi bombers approached the coast singly in the morning.

headline: THRILLING AIR BATTLES
body: Numerous German bombers, some with escorts of fighter planes, were engaged in battles by R.A.F. fighters in the English air defence area yesterday. Eight enemy aircraft are known to have been shot down during the day and others were damaged.
signals: ONLY TWO FIGHTERS LOST DEFENDING BRITAIN

headline: GREAT AIR BATTLE
body: It is officially stated that eleven German 'planes were shot down during to-day's series of engagements while a number of others are reported to have been destroyed. Two of our fighters were lost in to-day's combats and three yesterday.
signals: GERMANY PAYS DEARLY FOR RAID ON BRITAIN

headline: R.A.F. BOMBERS OVER GERMANY
body: The Air Ministry states that R.A.F. bombers last night attacked naval dockyards at Wilhelmshaven and Bremen, goods yards in the Ruhr, oil refineries at Monheim and aerodromes at Borkum, Texel, Schipol and Waalhaven.

headline: YESTERDAY'S TOTAL 23 'PLANES
body: It was officially announced at 8.15 this evening that the R.A.F. destroyed ten enemy bombers in to-day's operations. Two of our fighters are missing. Yesterday's total was twenty-three.
signals: R.A.F. CUTTING ROOTS OF INVASION PLANS

headline: COSTLY WEEK
body: LONDON, July 13. German bombers and fighters continued their attacks on shipping lanes and coastal areas today. Nine planes abortively attacked a ship lying outside a Channel port.

headline: FIERCE AIR BATTLE IN STRAITS OF DOVER
body: An Air Ministry communique states: 'Enemy aircraft which were attacking shipping in the Straits of Dover early this evening were intercepted and five of them, one fighter and four bombers, were shot down into the sea by our fighters.'

headline: THREE MORE RAIDERS DOWNED
body: It is officially stated that R.A.F. fighters shot down three bombers over the British coast this afternoon. A raider was seen over a town in the south-east area tonight.

headline: GERMAN RAIDERS SHOT DOWN
body: One Hurricane pilot shot down two Junkers into the English Channel this afternoon. Spitfires destroyed a Heinkel off the north-east coast of Scotland.
signals: R.A.F. RAIDS SERIOUSLY HAMPER GERMAN TRANSPORT

headline: LONE RAIDERS
body: Solitary German bombers attacked south-east Scotland and south-east England to-night. Both are believed to have been brought down, making the total four during the day and night.

headline: OVER 150 RAIDERS ATTACK BRITAIN
body: It is officially stated that over 150 German bombers were engaged in two battles on the south-east coast. The first battle occurred at noon, when 70 raiders attempted to bomb a convoy.
signals: R.A.F. BREAKS UP BIG BOMBING RAID ON CHANNEL

headline: 21 RAIDERS DOWN
body: It is now known that 21 German raiders were shot down round the British coasts yesterday. It was announced by the Air Ministry that nine more were destroyed than was originally reported. Another three raiders have been shot down to-day.

headline: HEAVY BLOWS BY R.A.F.
body: French airmen participated in R.A.F. raids over north-west Germany, states a communique from General de Gaulle's headquarters. The communique adds that in spite of violent opposition from the ground defences the objectives were attacked with success and all the French airmen returned safely.

headline: GERMANS LOSE FOUR RAIDERS
body: RUGBY, July 22. An Air Ministry communique issued to-day states: 'In yesterday's air battles round our coasts, four enemy aircraft in all were destroyed.' The anti-aircraft defences did effective work.
signals: GREAT AIR RAID DAMAGE IN GERMANY

headline: OVER 60 PLANES IN AIR BATTLE
body: Over sixty British and German fighters participated in a battle over the east coast this afternoon, in which two German fighters were shot down. The battle occurred when German bombers, escorted by fighters, attacked a convoy in the Thames Estuary.
signals: GERMANS LOSE TWELVE MORE PLANES IN LATEST RAIDS

headline: 100 PLANES IN LONGEST AIR BATTLE YET
body: Fierce attack on convoy foiled; nine raiders down. A great battle in which 100 planes participated followed an unsuccessful German attack on a convoy off the south-east coast.

headline: RECORD TOTAL OF PLANES SHOT DOWN
body: Great day for R.A.F.; bombs unloaded on towns by fugitive enemy raiders. It is now officially confirmed that 28 German 'planes were shot down yesterday in raids on Britain.

headline: R.A.F.'S WEEK-END TOTAL IN BATTLES OVER BRITAIN
body: Nine German planes were brought down around Britain to-day, five of them in a battle off the south-east coast. Two British fighters were lost, but the pilot of one is safe, though wounded. With the four enemy planes brought down yesterday, the week-end total is 13.
signals: BIG SCALE AIR STRAFE BY BRITISH

headline: 17 RAIDERS DESTROYED AT COST OF ONE BRITISH
body: Dover, on the south-east coast of England, was attacked by a large force of Nazi bombers protected by fighters this morning. British fighters and anti-aircraft guns went into action, and in the terrific battle which followed, in which it is estimated that 100 planes participated, the enemy lost 17 aircraft at the cost of one British fighter missing.

headline: NAZI PLANES HURLED BACK WITH HEAVY LOSSES
body: A surprise attack on the Channel port of Dover by 80 German planes to-day was hurled back with heavy losses to the raiders. The battle raged for half an hour, during which 18 German planes were shot down, two by anti-aircraft fire.
signals: HEAVY NAZI LOSSES IN ATTACK ON DOVER

headline: HEAVY TOLL OF NAZI 'PLANES LAST MONTH
body: A total of 240 German 'planes were destroyed during July, involving 600 officers and men killed or taken prisoner. Spitfires and Hurricanes went up when a German 'plane attacked shipping off the south-east of England.

headline: 40 BRITISH PLANES ENGAGE ENEMY RAIDERS
body: Forty British fighters engaged German planes over the Channel yesterday afternoon. A patrol of Hurricanes first intercepted a group of Messerschmitt fighters and bombers, after which stronger British forces arrived.

headline: RAIDERS OVER NAZI CAPITAL
body: LONDON, August 2. The Berlin correspondent of the Associated Press says the daily Foreign Office Press conference was dramatically interrupted when anti-aircraft guns, apparently situated on the roof of the Foreign Office, suddenly came into action. The Wilhelmstrasse artillery operated for the first time.

headline: WIDESPREAD GERMAN ATTACKS ON BRITAIN
body: Raiders were over England last night in the most widespread attack to date. The B.B.C. went off the air 'in the interests of national security' for half an hour. The skies over the south-east coastal areas blazed with a flash of guns, shell-bursts and searchlights.

headline: GERMAN OIL PLANT LEFT IN FLAMES
body: RUGBY, August 5. R.A.F. bombers last night attacked an oil plant at Sterkrade in the Ruhr, and considerable damage was done to the target, which was left in flames, says an Air Ministry communique issued to-day.

headline: THE BATTLE OF THE SKIES
body: When Goering boasted that for every bomb dropped on Germany by the British his bombers would drop ten in retaliation he meant it. Why he has not yet attempted to live up to his boast is best known to himself. We can be certain, however, that he is not inspired by any humanitarian motive.

headline: MANY IMPORTANT OBJECTIVES BOMBED
body: LONDON, August 6. The Air Ministry announced that the R.A.F. last night bombed objectives in Germany and Holland, including Wismar, Kiel, Hamburg and Hamm, and also aerodromes at Schipol and Borkum. Big scale operations by the R.A.F. continue.

headline: GERMAN RAIDERS ROUTED
body: German planes were off south-eastern England this afternoon. A number of small bombs were dropped near a small ship. The raiders fled when R.A.F. planes appeared.
signals: DAY AND NIGHT RAIDS BY R.A.F. BOMBERS

headline: GERMANY RESUMES RAIDS ON BRITAIN
body: Germany resumed air raids against Britain to-day, but after yesterday's costly adventure, kept her armadas aground, and used fast Messerschmitt fighters to make machine-gun attacks. Few bombers operated.

headline: DAY AND NIGHT: AIR RAIDS ON ENEMY
body: RUGBY, August 11. An Air Ministry communique states: 'R.A.F. bombers yesterday made a daylight attack on a number of enemy-occupied aerodromes in Holland and France.' A wide area was covered.

headline: BIG AIR BATTLES RAGING
body: It is officially stated that large-scale enemy activity is occurring over a wide area of the Channel and Thames Estuary. Enemy planes crossed the Kentish coast this morning. Bombs were dropped on several places near the coast.
signals: TWO LARGE-SCALE ATTACKS THWARTED EARLIER IN THE DAY

headline: GERMANS LOSE 61 PLANES IN MONDAY'S BATTLE
body: What are described as the biggest air battles of the war took place to-day when the Germans made large-scale raids over a wide area of the English Channel, the Thames Estuary, and the Kent and Sussex coasts.
signals: BOMB FOR BOMB: R.A.F. IS HITTING BACK

headline: GOERING'S HORDES FRUSTRATED BY R.A.F.
body: LONDON, August 14. To-day's air battle over the South-East Coast was one of the fiercest since the air offensive began. Spitfires and Hurricanes frustrated an attempt by 300 raiders to attack the coastal areas. The fierce thrust failed.

headline: CROYDON SINGLED OUT
body: Twenty to 30 raiders bombed Croydon this evening. Fighters shot down three. Bombs hit a hangar on the outskirts of the aerodrome and razed buildings.
signals: R.A.F. BATTLE WITH HUNDREDS OF NAZIS

headline: FIRST BOMBS ON LONDON
body: Massed air attack by Germans. It is officially stated that German raids over England to-day included the south-west suburbs of London and the Thames Estuary. Bombs were dropped, causing casualties and damage.
signals: RAIDERS SHOT DOWN AT RATE OF ONE A MINUTE

headline: RAIDERS CRASHED EACH MINUTE
body: A low-flying German fighter machine-gunned an army signal training unit on the south-east coast, but when it returned a second time the trainees were waiting with rifles and blazed away. The German reared up and crashed.

headline: THREE MASS RAIDS
body: It is now officially disclosed that two more R.A.F. pilots, making a total of twelve out of British fighters shot down yesterday, are safe. In all 144 enemy aircraft were destroyed.

headline: TONS OF BOMBS ON GERMANY
body: The Air Ministry says the R.A.F. dropped ten tons of high explosive bombs and numerous incendiary bombs in an attack on the extensive power station at Zschornwitz, 25 miles north of Leipsig, causing a great explosion and a series of fires.
signals: GERMAN RAIDS ON BRITAIN AGAIN ON SMALL SCALE

headline: LULL IN 'BATTLE FOR BRITAIN'
body: LONDON, August 20. Up to 9 p.m. the Royal Air Force destroyed seven air raiders against Britain. The Nazis show greater respect for the defences.
signals: LOSSES OF R.A.F. AIRMEN FIFTH OF ENEMY'S

headline: 13 GERMAN PLANES LOST IN HIT-AND-RUN RAIDS
body: Thirteen German planes were brought down over Britain to-day in a series of hit-and-run raids. There were no mass raids, but the Germans adopted the tactics they used in the earlier stages of the war.

headline: SHELLS ACROSS THE CHANNEL
body: Germany is not alone in firing shells across the Channel. British guns fired a few rounds into occupied France. The extent of the firing is not stated in the official communique, but is described as 'a few shells.'
signals: DARING R.A.F. RAID ON ITALIAN BASE
MADE BY ENEMY BOMBERS ON BRITAIN

headline: RAIDERS AGAIN OVER LONDON
body: LONDON, August 25. An Air Ministry communique states: reports up to 8 p.m. show that 39 enemy planes were shot down to-day, against 11 British.

headline: BERLIN BOMBED
body: It is stated officially that the Royal Air Force bombed armament factories in Berlin last night. The Berlin High Command admits an R.A.F. raid on Berlin and says it is the first since the outbreak of the war.

headline: NO SLACKENING IN AERIAL WARFARE
body: The persistent and almost continuous German air attacks on Britain go on by night and day. A raid on London last night lasted 375 minutes. Attacks were delivered also in the Midlands area, where fires were caused.

headline: INDUSTRIAL LIFE IS DISLOCATED
body: The dislocation of industrial life in Germany and damage to industrial plant, and, in particular, to German synthetic oil works, by repeated Royal Air Force attacks, is commented upon to-day in official circles in London.
signals: GERMAN OIL SUPPLY HARD HIT BY R.A.F.

headline: LONDON'S WORST, LONGEST DOSE OF BOMBING
body: Londoners went cheerfully to work this morning after the most severe and prolonged dose of bombing the capital has yet received. The King and Queen set an example of imperturbability on Tuesday night, when they refused to allow an air raid warning to interfere with their all-night journey to the Northern Command.

headline: FAILURE OF RAIDERS' TERROR TACTICS
body: An official of the Air Ministry, discussing last night's raids, emphasised the apparent uselessness which distinguished them. For example, he said, it was impossible to believe that the enemy could have had any specific targets in the London area in mind, and certainly no military objectives.

headline: 'HERE THEY ARE AGAIN!'
body: 'Here they are again,' commented thousands of Londoners going to work when the sirens broke through the roar of traffic this morning. The alarm resulted from the appearance of a dozen German bombers with an escort of 20 Messerschmitts over south-east England.
signals: WAR IN THE AIR GROWING IN INTENSITY

headline: THREE MASS RAIDS
body: On Monday, the last day of the first year of the war, the German air force made three unsuccessful mass attacks on Kent and Thames Estuary aerodromes. Fighter Command pilots shot down 38 enemy bombers and fighters, bringing their total of German raiders destroyed during the twelve months to 1771.
signals: NO RAIDERS OVER LONDON LAST NIGHT

headline: WAR'S SECOND YEAR BEGINS WITH RAID
body: An air raid warning was in force in the London area as the second year of war began at 11 a.m., says a British official wireless message. While the warning was still sounding, the King held an investiture at Buckingham Palace, when he decorated three V.C.'s.

headline: TERRIFIC BATTLE
body: A formation of enemy planes passed over a town not far from the Thames Estuary during London's morning alarm. British fighters routed a strong force of enemy raiders in a terrific battle over the south-east coastal district.
signals: GERMANS FAIL TO WEAKEN BRITISH FIGHTER OPPOSITION

headline: GERMAN BLITZKRIEG AGAINST BRITISH AERODROMES FAILS
body: It is authoritatively stated that the Blitzkrieg against R.A.F. aerodromes in south-east England has thus far failed to drive British fighter opposition from this corner of Britain nearest to the enemy. It is not denied that several advanced aerodromes have been severely hammered, but not one has been out of commission for longer than a very short time.

headline: BIG FORMATIONS CROSS THE KENTISH COAST
body: LONDON, September 6. According to an Air Ministry bulletin, British fighters were shooting down enemy aircraft which raided southern England this morning at the rate of one every two minutes. Bombs were jettisoned and homes destroyed.

headline: AIR WAR GROWS INTENSE
body: There is an unmistakable crescendo in the intensity of the war in the air. The latest R.A.F. raid on the German capital is the worst yet experienced by the Berliners. In other parts of Germany and German-occupied territory the British air offensive is being prosecuted with great energy and destructive effects.

headline: RUNNING BATTLES
body: Between 5 and 6 p.m. on Monday, after a morning of calm, Germany launched another 350 aircraft at south-east England and the London area. Successive waves of bombers and fighters crossed the coast between North Foreland and Hastings.

headline: THIRD NIGHT OF BLITZBOMBING
body: Thirty bombers escorted by waves of fighters crossed the south-east coast shortly after 5 p.m. and headed for London. Anti-aircraft guns put up a fierce barrage, as a result of which the bomber formation broke and turned seawards, rapidly losing height.

headline: FIERCE BARRAGE
body: Guns of all calibre have been used in a tremendous barrage which London is throwing up in to-night's battle against German raiders. There are practically no searchlights in action, and the battle is being fought out in the dark, except for great purple flashes from the guns which light the night sky.

headline: QUARTER DOWNED
body: The German air force again lost nearly a quarter of its raiders in a two-hour air battle over London and the south-east of England this Wednesday afternoon.
signals: BOND STREET AND BURLINGTON ARCADE DAMAGED
NEW TACTICS IN THE AIR WAR

headline: NEW ZEALAND PILOTS IN ACTION
body: LONDON, September 12. The British Air Ministry stated that New Zealand pilots participated when two squadrons of Hurricanes yesterday ferociously attacked a formation of 150 bombers bound for London and escorted by fighters.

headline: 263 RAIDERS DESTROYED
body: The week's blitzbombing has cost the Germans to midnight on Friday 263 planes, many of which were bombers with multiple crews. Britain lost 62 defending fighters, but many of the pilots and gunners were saved.

headline: MOST CRUSHING AIR DEFEAT
body: The German air force yesterday suffered its most devastating defeat of the war when great mass attacks on London and the south-east of England were smashed. It is officially announced that 185 German aircraft were destroyed and 25 British fighters were lost.
signals: DISASTROUS DAY FOR NAZI AIR FORCE

headline: TWELVE RAIDERS DOWN
body: RUGBY, 17th September. An Air Ministry communique issued on Wednesday at 1.40 a.m. says: 'Up to midnight five enemy bombers were shot down in attacks made in south-east England during darkness.' Tuesday's total over Britain was twelve.
signals: R.A.F. SUPERIORITY AND A.A. EFFICIENCY DEMONSTRATED

headline: ENEMY LOSE 42 PLANES IN DAYLIGHT
body: Forty-two enemy aircraft have been destroyed in engagements during the day. Nine R.A.F. fighters were lost but the pilots of five are safe. Air raid warnings have sounded eight times in the London area since dawn.

headline: MASS ATTACKS RESUMED
body: R.A.F. fighters meet the challenge; 46 Nazi planes down. A joint communique by the Air Ministry and Ministry of Home Security states: 'Enemy air activity today has been mainly confined to the south-eastern area.'

headline: INVASION BAULKED
body: Continuing their relentless hammering of the enemy's Channel ports, bomber squadrons of the R.A.F. last night again attacked shipping concentrations, docks, and harbour installations from Flushing in the north to Le Havre in the south-west. Le Havre was singled out for the night's heaviest bombardment.

headline: BOMBING OF LONDON UNABATED
body: The bombing blitzkrieg on London entered its third week with unabated fury. There was a nocturnal blasting from guns and bombs shortly after nightfall, providing the now familiar scene of completely empty streets and a sky lit by flashes, accompanied by heavy detonations.
signals: FEWER CASUALTIES AND LESS DAMAGE FROM AIR RAIDS

headline: 200 NAZI RAIDERS CHASED BACK HOME
body: Two hundred raiders in four formations tried to reach London by the Kent, Essex and Thames Estuary routes this morning. British fighters and anti-aircraft fire broke them up. Ten are reported to have been shot down.
signals: BOTH SIDES ACTIVE IN THE AIR

headline: TERRIFIC BARRAGE DRIVES BACK HUGE FLEET OF RAIDERS
body: After a break of only a few hours, Germany resumed the blitzkrieg against England this morning, when 100 bombers and fighters crossed the Kent coast. A huge formation of Germans was later seen proceeding up the Thames Estuary. It met with a terrific barrage, dogfights occurring as the raiders retreated, one fighter plunging into the sea.

headline: RAIDERS OVER CENTRAL LONDON
body: LONDON, September 25. Bombers concentrated on Central London early to-day. A number of people were killed or injured when what is believed to have been an aerial torpedo landed outside a restaurant, demolishing the hotel opposite and also shattering a number of buildings in the neighbourhood.

headline: R.A.F. ATTACKS HEART OF BERLIN
body: A number of military objectives in the heart of Berlin were singled out and attacked on Tuesday night when R.A.F. heavy bombers, for the second night in succession, carried the war into the German capital in a raid lasting two and a-half hours.

headline: 130 SHOT DOWN BY R.A.F. FIGHTERS
body: The Air Ministry announced that up to 10.30 p.m. to-day 130 enemy aircraft were destroyed. The R.A.F. had lost 34 fighters, but the pilots of 15 were safe.
signals: DESPERATE GERMAN ATTACKS WRECKED ON ROCK OF R.A.F. DEFENCES

headline: SUICIDAL MASS ATTACKS
body: Many raiders were shot down over London's breakfast tables yesterday when the Germans made suicidal attempts at daylight raids which began less than four hours after the conclusion of the usual night onslaught. A series of thrashings inflicted on the Luftwaffe resulted in 133 of the raiders being destroyed, compared with British losses of 34 planes and 18 pilots.
signals: ANOTHER SUCCESSFUL DAY FOR THE R.A.F.

headline: DESTRUCTION OF 47 DAYLIGHT ATTACKERS
body: R.A.F. fighters and anti-aircraft defences were constantly in action to-day, in the course of which the enemy made four large scale attacks on south and south-east England. It is officially stated that up to 8 p.m. 47 enemy aircraft had been destroyed.

headline: RAIDERS THROWN BACK
body: London's big guns, which have been throwing back many German raiders each night ever since the air war began, tonight succeeded in driving them off altogether for a time. Surprised Londoners in beds and shelters heard the all-clear round about midnight.
signals: NIGHT RAIDERS FAIL TO REACH CENTRAL LONDON

headline: 1000 DAYLIGHT RAIDERS ROUTED BY BRILLIANT R.A.F. DEFENCE
body: There have been many astonishing happenings in the daylight attacks against Britain, but none more remarkable than today's. Within a few hours enemy machines totalling nearly 1000 desperately attempted to reach Central London. Great waves followed one another at short intervals and sought by sheer weight of numbers to overwhelm the defences.
signals: FEW DAY RAIDERS ABLE TO REACH LONDON

headline: BERLIN BOMBED FOR OVER AN HOUR
body: Sirens aroused Berliners from their sleep early this morning, says a Berlin cable message. They were forced to stay in their shelters for 72 minutes. The raiders concentrated on the north-west industrial area, where explosions were continuous.

headline: NAZI RAIDERS IMPEDED BY CHANNEL STORMS
body: After a quiet morning, free from enemy attack, three alerts were sounded this afternoon. In the first raid, four houses were damaged in east London, while in the second strike, in the north of the city, some people were injured in a block of flats when a high-explosive bomb fell in the street.
signals: BAD WEATHER GIVES LONDON QUIETER DAY

headline: LONDON'S QUIETEST NIGHT
body: London is having its quietest night in the four weeks since the aerial blitzkrieg was launched on the capital. During the day bad weather hampered the raiders and attacks were on a much smaller scale if over a wider area than usual.

headline: THRILLING BATTLES OVER BRITAIN
body: London had six 'alerts' during today. More thrilling air battles occurred this morning when several groups of German planes crossed the Kent coast. British fighters broke up the formations, which scattered in disorder.

headline: GREAT BERLIN RAID
body: Referring to last night's R.A.F. raid on Berlin, the Air Ministry states that more than 100 heavy bombs were dropped on three main power stations in the capital. Large fires were started in the Tempelhof goods yards.
signals: BERLIN BOMBED FOR OVER FOUR HOURS

headline: LONDON BOMBED IN DAYLIGHT RAID
body: LONDON, October 9. London has had two alerts today. A number of German raiders were over London this afternoon during the second alert.

headline: A LIVELY NIGHT
body: German attacks on Britain since nightfall on Thursday have been widespread. The battles of the air were heralded by long-range German gunfire across the Straits of Dover.
signals: NAZI RAIDERS SCATTERED BY BRITISH FIGHTERS
CHANNEL GUNS OPEN NAZI NIGHT ATTACK

headline: TERRIFIC ATTACK ON GERMAN GUNS
body: Strong forces of R.A.F. bombers inflicted terrific punishment on a battery of four long-range guns beside the Cap Gris Nez lighthouse after they shelled the Dover area for half-an-hour. At dusk the cliff watchers saw a giant tongue of flame through the mist enshrouding the French shore when a shell burst with a terrific explosion.

headline: HEAVIEST YET DROPPED ON GERMANY
body: When the R.A.F. raided Germany on Saturday night they carried with them the heaviest bombs they have ever used on Germany, a B.B.C. broadcast states. One of the places where some of the bombs were dropped was Krupps' factory at Essen.
signals: HAMBURG HAS MOST VIOLENT RAID YET

headline: HEART OF BERLIN AGAIN BOMBED BY R.A.F.
body: An Air Ministry communique issued early this afternoon describes how on Saturday night strong forces of R.A.F. bombers continued their offensive against military objectives in Germany and enemy-occupied territory.

headline: R.A.F. PILOT DOWNS FOUR HUNS IN TEN MINUTES
body: A flight lieutenant who recently won a bar to his D.F.C. for destroying eight German raiders during eight days in the defence of London has achieved a new personal record, shooting down four Messerschmitts in 10 minutes. He went up with his Hurricane squadron to attack a force of Messerschmitt 109 fighters which the Germans are now using as bombers in daylight attacks on London.
signals: ENEMY USES NEW TYPE OF BOMB

headline: R.A.F. BOMBERS AGAIN STRIKE AT BERLIN
body: Last night R.A.F. bombers again struck at Berlin and other targets in Germany and German-occupied territory. Several important military objectives in Berlin were effectively bombed. Attacks were also made on oil plants at Stettin and Magdeburg.
signals: FOUR PLANES DOWN IN TEN MINUTES

headline: GREAT DAMAGE IN FOUR-HOUR RAID
body: The naval dockyards at Kiel and oil supply centres inside Germany were the principal objectives of the R.A.F. heavy bomber squadrons last night. Many other targets in Germany and German-occupied territory included aluminium factories, docks, railways and aerodromes.

headline: ENEMY BASES SUFFER
body: LONDON, October 18. During the 10 days from October 5 to October 15 Royal Air Force bombers have attacked military targets at 52 different places in Germany. A daylight attack was made on Brest.
signals: R.A.F. OVER HAMBURG, KIEL AND BREMEN

headline: FIVE MASS RAIDS ON LONDON THWARTED
body: A yellow-nosed Messerschmitt was shot down in a London street during an air battle this afternoon. There were terrific dogfights during the Germans' five ineffectual attempts to reach London in attempted mass raids.

headline: GREAT RAID ON BERLIN
body: RUGBY, October 21. Both ends of the Rome-Berlin Axis had a foretaste of the gathering strength of the R.A.F. last night when the capital of the German Reich and two of Italy's great industrial centres were simultaneously attacked by aircraft of the Bomber Command, says the Air Ministry News Service.
signals: FIVE MASS RAIDS ON LONDON THWARTED
GREAT BOMBING ATTACKS: LONG BERLIN RAID

headline: HAMMER BLOW AT BERLIN
body: R.A.F. strikes again; both ends of the Axis feel the weight of British air power. RUGBY, October 21. The capital of the German Reich and two of Italy's great industrial centres were simultaneously attacked by aircraft of the Bomber Command on Sunday night.

headline: NAZI SHIPYARDS CRIPPLED BY R.A.F.
body: It is officially stated that, although adverse weather considerably hampered operations, R.A.F. bombers again attacked objectives in Germany last night. Enemy warships under construction at the Blohm and Voss yards at Hamburg were heavily attacked.
signals: NAZI PLANES SLACKEN TEMPO OF THEIR ATTACKS

headline: R.A.F. SET SEA ALIGHT WITH NEW BOMB
body: The Zurich newspaper Volkrecht, quoting travellers from Holland, says that Royal Air Force raiders against barge concentrations on the Rhine and the Scheldt used thousands of incendiary bombs, consisting of a special mixture of oil, phosphorus and magnesium, which burned on the water, transforming the estuaries into a sea of flame and igniting barges.

headline: R.A.F. GIVES BERLIN ANOTHER WARM TIME
body: Flames lit up a great stretch of sky over Berlin last night when, for the second night in succession, R.A.F. planes raided the German capital. The Germans admit that British planes flew continuously over the centre of the city. Poor visibility forced the R.A.F. to fly low and the machines singled out vital targets to cause extensive damage.

headline: R.A.F. BOMBS BERLIN FOR 23RD TIME
body: R.A.F. bombers heavily raided Berlin on Thursday night for the second night in succession. It was the 23rd raid made on the German capital.

headline: HUN RAIDERS RECEIVE A SEVERE HANDLING
body: Enemy planes were reported over many parts of the country to-day. The Bishop of London disclosed that 32 London churches have been destroyed or rendered unusable and 47 seriously damaged.

headline: 160 RAIDERS ATTEMPT TO REACH LONDON
body: About 160 raiders, mostly fighter-bombers, tried to reach London during three alerts to-day. A very small proportion penetrated the outer defences.

headline: NEW, INTENSE BARRAGE GREETS LONDON RAIDERS
body: Raiders attempting to reach London last night stumbled on a new and intensive anti-aircraft barrage, covering a popular route across the south-east coast. The barrage is reported to be most effective, and engaged planes for a considerable distance.
